question.text: Under the current single-bond cash-settled GOI Interest Rate Futures (6-year, 10-year and 13-year), the underlying is best described as:

answer.text: A specific GOI dated security selected by the exchanges, with one lot equal to 2,000 notional bonds of face value Rs. 100 each (notional FV Rs. 2 lakh per lot), settled in cash
A hypothetical bond that does not exist and cannot be traded in any market
A bond newly issued by RBI specifically for futures settlement purposes
A basket of deliverable GOI bonds, with settlement against the cheapest-to-deliver bond

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series IV pp.105, 112 and 115-116 describe the current cash-settled 6/10/13-year GOI Interest Rate Futures: the underlying is a single real GOI dated security selected by the exchanges, one lot is 2,000 notional bonds of FV Rs. 100 each (i.e. notional FV Rs. 2 lakh per lot), and the contract is cash-settled. Option A captures all three features. The Trap: Option B describes a purely fictitious bond - the underlying is a real GOI security. Option C is incorrect because RBI does not issue special bonds for futures. Option D describes the old 2009-framework notional 7% 10-year contract with a cheapest-to-deliver basket, which was discontinued when the single-bond, cash-settled IRF design was introduced. In the original ambiguous version the keyed answer described "actual settlement on a specific real bond", which conflated cash settlement with physical settlement and conflated the old and new IRF frameworks. Note: The original question was ambiguous because the stem mixed the old notional-bond / CTD framework with the current cash-settled single-bond IRF, and the keyed answer was not strictly consistent with either. The stem has been narrowed to the current single-bond cash-settled IRF, and option A spells out the underlying, lot size and cash settlement so it is uniquely correct. Source: NISM Series IV, Dec 2025, pp.105, 112, 115-116.
